builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CG-Probes: Recovering Guardrail Directions from Patient Query Embeddings
summary: The method replaces per-query LLM-based risk classification with difference-in-means linear probes over frozen query embeddings, scored along clinician-defined ordinal axes. It costs an offline clustering and contrastive-pair generation pipeline (BERTopic plus few-shot prompting over ~80k queries), embedding lookups at inference, and clinician time to define axes and set thresholds; per-query cost is negligible. It can fail because the topic-sensitivity axis was not recoverable as a linear direction, the evaluation covered only 200 Czech oncology queries, and robustness to new queries, new axes, and other domains remains unvalidated.
rationale: The approach runs on constrained infrastructure and is cheap to serve, but its validated scope is narrow and axis-dependent, so the reader should validate it on their own queries and risk axes before production use.
technique: Linear risk probes on frozen embeddings

claims.statement: The method replaces per-query LLM-based risk classification with difference-in-means linear probes over frozen query embeddings, scored along clinician-defined ordinal axes. It costs an offline clustering and contrastive-pair generation pipeline (BERTopic plus few-shot prompting over ~80k queries), embedding lookups at inference, and clinician time to define axes and set thresholds; per-query cost is negligible. It can fail because the topic-sensitivity axis was not recoverable as a linear direction, the evaluation covered only 200 Czech oncology queries, and robustness to new queries, new axes, and other domains remains unvalidated.
Probes are competitive with open-weight LLMs (no significant difference in quadratic-weighted kappa) at a fraction of the latency; no specific latency factor is reported.
